## Task Allocation

In a list, provide your name and which task you completed

## Reproducible Data Science

### The Importance of Reproducible Research: Main Steps

You should always show, how you got to the results of your research, so other people can check your research and reproduce it. They could potentially also
create new experiments based on your work, which means they need to be able to understand your reasoning and the steps you took to get to your results. 
The UZH has a center for [Reproducable Science](!https://www.crs.uzh.ch/en.html) that provides help and instructions on how to conduct reproducable science and research.


### Open Science and FAIR Data Principles

Summarise the main principles of Open Science and explain what FAIR Data Principles stand for. Explain the main steps one should take to make their work reproducible.

### Resources and Platforms 

Provide brief descriptions and links to the resources that one could use to make their work reproducible.


## The Art (and Science) of Plotting

### Plot Types

Provide an overview of the main plot types (including visual examples) and explain which types of data are best suited for each kind of plot.

### Colour Palettes

Explain how to use colour palettes effectively, which types of palettes are best suited to different kinds of data, and what factors should be considered when selecting an appropriate colour scheme.

### Plotting Tools and Resources

Here, you should include links and brief descriptions of platforms and software for data visualization and colour palette selection, as well as useful R packages for plotting and styling graphics.
